intro.text: These terms apply when you use Chalkie Chalkie, the online whiteboard for tutoring at chalkiechalkie.com (the 'Services'). Please read them before you create an account or buy a plan.
Chalkie Chalkie is run by Harrison Baghurst, a sole trader based in the United Kingdom, trading as Chalkie Chalkie ('we', 'us', or 'our'). You can contact us by email at {{CONTACT_EMAIL}}.

**In short:** tutors pay a monthly plan to run lessons on a shared whiteboard, and students use it free of charge. You must be 13 or over to have an account and 18 or over to buy a plan. You can cancel whenever you like from Settings. If you are a consumer, nothing in these terms takes away your legal rights.

blocks.text: By creating an account you agree to these terms. Our [Privacy Policy](/privacy-policy) and [Cookie Policy](/cookie-policy) explain how we handle your personal information and do not form part of this contract.

We may update these terms, for example to reflect changes in the law or in the Services. If a change materially affects you, we will email you at least 30 days before it takes effect. If you do not agree to the change, you can cancel your plan or delete your account before then.
We recommend you save or print a copy of these terms for your records.

Chalkie Chalkie lets tutors schedule lessons ('workspaces') and teach them on a shared whiteboard with their students in real time. Everyone in a workspace can draw, highlight, erase, move items and add images and PDFs to the board.
Tutors need a paid plan to create workspaces and link with students. Students do not need a plan and never pay us: their tutor's plan covers every lesson they are invited to.
The whiteboard is designed for desktop and laptop browsers. We provide the Services with reasonable care and skill, and as described on our website and in these terms.

items: You must be **13 or over** to create an account.
If you are under 18, you must have the agreement of a parent or guardian to use the Services. A parent or guardian may also create and manage an account on their child's behalf.
You must be **18 or over** to buy a plan.
An account is for one person. Give accurate details, keep your sign-in secure, and tell us straight away if you think someone else has used your account.

blocks.text: If we find that an account belongs to someone under 13, we will close it and delete its data.
Tutors link with students using a link code and invite linked students to workspaces. A workspace is visible only to the people its tutor has invited.

**We provide a tool, not a tutoring service.** We do not employ, recommend, vet or check tutors, and we are not a party to any arrangement between a tutor and their students or their families, including any fees for lessons.
If you are a tutor, you are responsible for your lessons and for how you use the Services with your students. In particular, you are responsible for:

items: getting the agreement of a parent or guardian before teaching anyone under 18 through the Services;
your own safeguarding practices, and holding any DBS or other checks your tutoring work requires;
what you and your students put on the boards in your workspaces.

blocks.text: Parents and guardians should decide what supervision is right for their child during lessons.
Plans and prices

We offer Basic, Plus and Pro plans. What each plan includes and what it costs are shown on our [pricing page](/pricing) when you buy it, and that description forms part of your contract with us. All prices are in pounds sterling and **include VAT**.
Who takes your payment

Payments are handled by Stripe Managed Payments. Stripe, through its Link service, acts as the merchant of record for your purchase: it takes your payment, charges and accounts for VAT, sends your receipts, and provides billing support. Link's own terms, shown at checkout, also apply to your payment. We never see or store your full card details.
Renewal

Plans are monthly subscriptions. Your plan renews automatically, and you are charged at the start of each monthly billing period on your billing date, until you cancel. Your next payment date is shown in Settings.
Changing plan

items: **Upgrading now:** your new plan starts immediately and is charged in full today for a whole month, and your billing date moves to today. What you have already paid for the current month is not refunded or credited. We show you both amounts before you confirm.
**Upgrading from your next billing date:** you keep your current plan until then, and the new plan is charged on your usual billing date. Nothing is charged today.

**Downgrading:** your current plan continues until the end of the period you have paid for, and the lower plan takes over from your next billing date. Nothing is refunded for the rest of the current period.

blocks.text: A change of plan applies to everything already in your account, not just what you create afterwards. On a lower plan, workspaces are kept for less time, and any linked students over your new plan's limit are deactivated, most recently linked first.
Failed payments

If a payment fails, Stripe will retry it and you keep everything your plan allows while it does. If the retries fail, your plan is paused, meaning your lessons stop opening, until the payment goes through or the subscription ends. You can update your card through Link.
Price changes
We will email you at least 30 days before a price change applies to your subscription. If you do not want to pay the new price, you can cancel before it takes effect.
Cancelling your plan

You can cancel at any time from Settings, or through Link. Your plan stays active until the end of the period you have already paid for, and no further payments are taken. Until then, you can undo the cancellation from Settings with Keep plan.
Full refund within 14 days

If you change your mind within 14 days of first buying a plan, you can cancel and get a **full refund**, without giving a reason and however much you have used the Services. This covers your legal right to cancel as a consumer. To ask for it, email us at {{CONTACT_EMAIL}} or contact Link support, saying that you want to cancel. We will make sure you receive the refund within 14 days of telling us, to your original payment method.
Your plan ends when the refund is made, and section 7 then applies.
Other refunds

Apart from the 14-day refund, and your rights if the Services are faulty (see section 14), payments are not refunded for part of a billing period, including when you cancel, downgrade or delete your account.
When a plan ends, whether because you cancelled or because payment could not be taken:

items: your lessons stop opening, for you and your students;
you can no longer create workspaces or add students;
your links to students are deactivated;
your workspaces are kept for up to 30 days and then deleted permanently, unless you subscribe again before then.

blocks.text: A lesson that is already under way when a plan ends is allowed to finish.

Each workspace, including its board, drawings, images and PDFs, is deleted automatically once it has been kept for the period its tutor's plan allows after the lesson. The periods are shown on our [pricing page](/pricing).
The Services are not a backup or archive. Keep your own copies of anything you want to keep.

You keep ownership of everything you draw, write or upload ('your content'). You give us permission to store, copy, process and display your content only as far as we need to provide the Services to you and to the other people in your workspaces. This permission ends when your content is deleted, apart from copies held for a short time in backups.
Everything on a workspace's board can be seen by everyone invited to that workspace.
You must only upload content you have the right to share. Do not upload other people's personal information unless it is needed for the lesson and you are allowed to share it.
You must not use the Services to:

items: break the law, or share content that is illegal;
share sexual, violent, hateful or self-harm content, or anything else that is harmful to children;
bully, harass, threaten or groom anyone, or contact a child for any purpose other than genuine tutoring;
infringe anyone's copyright or other rights;
impersonate anyone, or share your account, sign-in or link codes publicly;
upload malware, or attempt to access accounts, workspaces or systems you have not been invited to;
scrape, overload or disrupt the Services, or get around plan limits, rate limits or security measures;
resell or provide the Services to others as your own product.

blocks.text: If you see content or behaviour on the Services that worries you, including anything that could put a child at risk, use **Report a concern**. You will find it on the flag button in a whiteboard's participant list, in the menu on each workspace in your dashboard, in Settings under Help, and at the bottom of every page, where you can use it without an account. You can also email us at {{CONTACT_EMAIL}}. Reports come to us, never to the person being reported. We review every report and may remove content or restrict, suspend or close accounts.
**If a child is in immediate danger, call 999.** You can also report concerns about online sexual abuse or grooming to [CEOP](https://www.ceop.police.uk).
If you disagree with a decision we have made about your content or account, email us and we will review it.

We may suspend or close an account, or remove content, if the account holder seriously or repeatedly breaks these terms, if we are required to by law, or if we reasonably need to in order to protect other users, especially children. We will tell you why, and give you notice first where it is reasonable to do so.
If we close a paid account when you have not broken these terms, we will refund the part of the current billing period you have paid for but not used.
If we decide to stop providing the Services altogether, we will give you at least 30 days' notice by email and refund any period you have paid for but not used.
Deleting your account

You can delete your account at any time from Settings. Deletion is immediate and cannot be undone: any plan is cancelled straight away, the workspaces you host are deleted, and you are removed from workspaces you joined. The unused part of your billing period is not refunded, but this does not affect your right to a full refund within 14 days of first buying a plan.

sections.heading: 13. Availability and changes to the Services

blocks.text: We aim to keep the Services available, but they may sometimes be interrupted for maintenance, updates or problems outside our control. We will try to keep interruptions short and to plan maintenance outside common lesson times.

We may change, add or remove features to improve the Services or to meet legal requirements. If a change significantly reduces what your paid plan gives you, we will tell you in advance, and you can cancel and receive a refund for any period you have paid for but not used.

sections.heading: 14. Our responsibility for loss or damage

blocks.text: Your legal rights

If you are a consumer, the Consumer Rights Act 2015 says the Services must be provided with reasonable care and skill and as described. If they are not, you can ask us to put things right or, if we cannot, to give you some or all of your money back. For more information, visit [Citizens Advice](https://www.citizensadvice.org.uk).
What we are responsible for

We are responsible for loss or damage you suffer that is a foreseeable result of us breaking these terms or failing to use reasonable care and skill. Loss or damage is foreseeable if it is obvious that it will happen, or if we both knew it might happen when you agreed to these terms. We are not responsible for loss or damage that is not foreseeable.

If digital content we supply damages a device or digital content belonging to you, and this is caused by our failure to use reasonable care and skill, we will either repair the damage or pay you compensation.
What we do not limit

Nothing in these terms limits or excludes our liability for death or personal injury caused by our negligence, for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation, or for anything else that cannot be limited or excluded by law, including your rights as a consumer.
If you use the Services for a business

If you use the Services in the course of a business, such as a tutoring business, we are not liable to you for any loss of profit, revenue, business or opportunity, and our total liability to you is limited to the amount you paid us in the 12 months before the event that caused the loss.

The Services, including our software, design, name and logo, belong to us. We give you a personal, non-transferable permission to use the Services in line with these terms. You must not copy, modify or distribute the Services, except as the law allows.
If you have a complaint, email us at {{CONTACT_EMAIL}}. We aim to reply within 14 days and will try to resolve it fairly. Complaints about a payment or refund can also be raised with Link support.

items: We may transfer our rights and obligations under these terms to another organisation. We will tell you if this happens, and if you are unhappy with the transfer you can cancel and receive a refund for any period you have paid for but not used.
You may only transfer your rights under these terms to someone else with our written agreement.
This contract is between you and us. No one else has any rights to enforce its terms.
If a court finds part of these terms unlawful, the rest will continue in force.
If we do not insist straight away that you do something you are required to do, or we delay taking steps against you, that does not stop us doing so later.

sections.heading: 18. Which laws apply and where you can bring claims

blocks.text: These terms are governed by the law of England and Wales. You can bring legal proceedings in the courts of England and Wales. If you live in Scotland, you can bring proceedings in Scotland or in England and Wales, and if you live in Northern Ireland, in Northern Ireland or in England and Wales.
If you live elsewhere, you also keep any protection given to you by the mandatory consumer laws of the country where you live.
